verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. Same conclusion — a uniform integer Δ_max bounding |i(ℓ)−i(ℓ′)| whenever |ℓ−ℓ′| ≤ 4 — reached through a different middle quantity. The two sides agree on the covering index itself: nativeArgument_expanded is exactly ((1+h)ℓ log 2 − 2 log ℓ)/log T_g with T_g = coverGrowth = 4+√2, and nativeIndex is its floor, so the ((1+h)ℓ log 2)-part contributes 4(1+h) log 2 in both. They differ in how the −2 log ℓ part is controlled. The paper uses the mean value theorem under the standing hypothesis ℓ ≥ ℓ₀, giving the term 8/ℓ₀ (= 2 · 4/ℓ₀); the Lean (log_level_gap, NavierStokes/SlotColoring.lean:342, |log n − log m| ≤ log 5 for n,m ≥ 1 with |n−m| ≤ 4) uses the ratio bound instead, giving 2 log 5 ≈ 3.219 in nativeGapBudget. Neither constant implies the other: the Lean needs only n,m ≥ 1 (no ℓ₀ threshold at all, so its hypotheses are weaker), but its constant is fixed, whereas the paper's 8/ℓ₀ is sharper for every ℓ₀ ≥ 3 and tends to 0. The flooring allowance also differs in shape: the paper writes 1 + (…) and then takes an integer upper bound, the Lean writes nativeGap = ⌈(…)⌉₊ + 1, which is at most one larger. The paper's displayed inequality with 8/ℓ₀ in it is therefore not what was checked. The surrounding result is unaffected: the only property used downstream is that Δ_max is one finite integer independent of the band (PartitionedCovariance.lean:243–248 consumes nativeIndex_gap solely to produce Δ = i(M)−i(L) ≤ nativeGap h as the hypothesis n ≤ D of centers_avoid_covering).
